summary: Import-time execution of obfuscated payload hidden in package.json with CI/sandbox evasion
details: index.js (the declared main entry) reads an undocumented _bz byte array (195 bytes beginning with the zlib magic 0x78 0x9c) from package.json, zlib-inflates it, and executes the decoded string via the Function constructor at require() time, running with full Node privileges in any process that imports the package. Execution is gated by an explicit early return when any of CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, or SANDBOX environment variables is set, and errors are swallowed by a try/catch, so the payload fires only in developer or production environments and stays silent under common analysis contexts. Smuggling the executable blob as a numeric byte array inside package.json rather than a.js file hides it from file-level review and from scanners that only inspect JavaScript sources. The package exports nothing useful and is described generically as a 'utility', providing no legitimate reason for this pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
